terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Static fence panel that tiles post to post. Both faces are seen and nothing is hollow, but nothing opens, turns or swings, so every part is fixed and one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. A level builder places these in runs of dozens, so the draw-call ceiling is the design constraint. ONE POST PER TILE: the post sits on the -X end and the bay runs to the +X edge, so tiles chain post-bay-post-bay along X with no doubled post at a joint. A village garden fence. Bamboo bleached silver-grey with darker nodes, black mould at the lashings, a few broken strips.

reasoning: ONE whole-bamboo post on the -X end (its top a hollow cut culm), a top and bottom rail lashed to its front with wound cord (three turns on the rail, two collars and a diagonal figure-of-eight on the post), a thin lath under the top rail, and a woven split-bamboo panel between the rails built as staggered sections: horizontal bands above and below a window band of vertical strip bundles with THREE openings -- a 0.13 m slot at 0.26, a 0.29 m window at 0.74 and a 0.20 m window at 1.38 of the 1.84 m bay, read off the plate as backdrop runs 307-347, 457-548 and 657-718 px in a 575 px bay (the proxy fused them into two).

TWO materials: split-bamboo weave (a 16-strip tile, 2.8 cm strips with tones 0.44..1.0, strong joints, grain and mould, rotated on the bands and upright on the bundles; no crossing bands, the plate's strips run unbroken and the weave is the section seams) and whole culm (a tile mapped around-by-along each cylinder with two node rings per 0.6 m on the post and per 1.0 m on the rails, grain, drying splits and near-black mould sheets below the nodes). Cord and the bore are vertex colours on the culm material.
No repetition system: the sections are one merge per strip direction; the fourteen cord rings ride the frame merge.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one box collider on the frame root, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is fat round culms with nodes, wound cord lashings, a hollow cut post top and a woven panel of staggered sections with three openings; the culm nodes, mould and strip joints are canvas, the openings, section stagger, lath, bore and every turn of cord are geometry.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 2.00 x 1.50 x 0.21 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The ONLY mechanism this prop has. Static fence geometry: nothing opens, turns or swings, so every part is fixed and gets no axis. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box: one proxy over the whole panel envelope, which is what a run of fence collides as.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center at ground, +Y up, +Z the FRONT face (the face the plate shows), +X along the run. The panel tiles post to post along X.

silhouette.description: One post 0.13 m round at x -0.927, 1.50 m tall, open at the top with a 7 cm bore; rails 0.12 m round at 0.21 and 1.30 m from the post's outer edge to the tile edge, centred 8 cm in front of the post axis; a 0.066 m lath at 1.21 m; woven sections 0.03 m thick from 0.27 to 1.17 m between x -0.853 and +0.99, with a slot 0.13 m wide and windows 0.29 and 0.20 m wide, all 0.51..0.96 m tall.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -1.00 at the lashing cord (the one post, 0.13 m round, centred at -0.927) to +1.00 at the rail ends, flush with the tile edge; y 0.00 to 1.50 at the post top; z -0.065 (post back) to +0.14 (rail fronts, lashed 4.5 cm into the post front). Measured on the plate: the right post spans 700 px for 1.50 m (466 px/m) and is 65 px wide (0.14 m); rails 55-73 px (0.12-0.15 m); the lath under the top rail 34 px (0.07 m); the stack at column x=690 gives rail 0.15..0.27, band 0.27..0.51, window 0.51..0.96, band 0.96..1.17, lath 1.17..1.24, rail 1.24..1.36. The proxy normalises to w/h 1.240 against the declared 1.333 and d/h 0.105 (0.16 m, Meshy having smoothed the rail into the post) against the built 0.137; the declared width is built and the band residual (mean |delta width| 0.089) is the declared aspect.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to w/h 1.240, d/h 0.105. Its front depth map (scratch/bamboo-fence-panel/_ev/front.png) shows two rails lashed over a thin panel with two dark openings and a mullion between; occupancy reads the openings at 0.38-0.62 H. The plate's backdrop-pixel scan (three openings, 0.51..0.96 m) overrides the proxy here: Meshy fused the narrow slot into its bundle and shrank the windows.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.80: the weave is the same both faces; the rails are on the front only, as the plate shows.

componentTree.name: Post, rails, lath and lashings
componentTree.topologyRationale: One open post with its rim, bore and foot as lathes, two rails, a lath and fourteen cord tori: one merge, one draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Post r 0.065 at x -0.927, 1.50 m, open-ended with an 11 mm rim and a 7 cm dark bore; rails r 0.06 at 0.21 and 1.30 m from x -0.992 to +1.00 at z 0.08; lath r 0.033 at 1.212 m, z 0.07; per joint three cord turns on the rail 18-42 mm off the post, collars 22 mm above and below the rail, and two diagonals tilted 0.95 rad about X.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Rails are buried 4.5 cm into the post front as interpenetrating solids; the rim annulus sits on the open cylinder's top ring and the bore floor 7 cm below; cord stands 6-8 mm proud; the lath overlaps the rail by 5 mm.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry; each cylinder carries culm UVs (u around, v along, 0.6 m per tile on the post and 1.0 m on the rails, phased per culm) so the node rings cross every culm at real spacing.

localFeatures.delivery: open cylinder with rim, bore and foot lathes

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Culm as vertex white, cord and bore as dark vertex colours, one culm canvas mapped around-by-along.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Top band y 0.96..1.174, bottom band 0.27..0.51, 0.03 m thick, from x -0.853 (the post face) to +0.99; the bottom-left section carries a #efece7 vertex tint for its mould.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Neighbouring sections alternate z by 3 mm, so no two co-facing faces share a plane; the vertical bundles stand 3-6 mm proud again.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: Rotated panel UVs at 0.45 m per tile.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Bamboo canvas rotated so the strips run horizontal.

geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: 3-6 mm proud of the neighbouring horizontal sections on both faces; never planar with them.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/weave.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.860. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.evidence: Fine strip joints, grain and dark mould across the weave in region-weave; the canvas draws them per strip.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-weave (0.860) at #b1aca5 and region-strips (0.804) at #aca7a1. The retuned strip canvas multiplies at a mean of ~0.77 (tones 0.44..1.0 with a pale tail), so the envelope is carried at #e6dfd6; the rendered top band measures luma 148 against the plate's 146.5 in a matched crop.

Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px canvas after construction as map and bumpMap -- 16 strips of varied width per 0.45 m (2.8 cm, the plate's 2.5-3 cm) with per-strip silver/warm-grey tone, the round of each strip, 14-24 longitudinal grain hairlines, lengthwise weathering patches, no crossing bands, and six mould clusters.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 2,772/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries, two canvases at 2.7 MB. Turntable: the three openings are real, allowed on measurement; collapse ratio passed as the built depth over width (0.105).

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Three components, no repetition system: 3 of 4.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 2,772 of 4,000: four cylinders, three lathes, fourteen cord tori (168 each), twelve boxes.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Cylinders and lathes for the culms, tori for the cord, boxes for the woven sections.
No InstancedMesh: nothing repeats at one size.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Every material is declared textureless. Two 512 px canvases after construction (weave, culm), 2.7 MB of texture VRAM.

risks.description: At 90 degrees the open +X end is a 0.03 m weave edge, a lath end and two 0.12 m rail ends, near the segmenter's 3.5% floor; that azimuth may report unsegmented (270, the post end, segments).
risks.mitigation: A property of a one-post tile seen from its open end; 0/180 segment at 0.99. Recorded, not bypassed.
